text: Works as a drop-in replacement for npm on existing projects with no migration or rewrites
quote: pnpm is a drop-in replacement for npm. Point it at any existing project — no migration, no rewrites, no lockfile gymnastics.

text: Persistent patches for dependency bugs via a patch command, reapplied on every install
quote: Fix a bug in a package without waiting for upstream — "pn patch" writes a persistent patch that is reapplied on every install.

text: Install and pin Node.js per project without nvm or shell hooks
quote: Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.

text: Strict node_modules layout: code can only import dependencies it declares
quote: A package can access only dependencies that are specified in its `package.json`.

text: Monorepo support with workspace protocol, filtered task runs, and a single shared lockfile
quote: First-class monorepos: the workspace protocol for local packages, filtering to run tasks on just the projects you touched, and a single lockfile for everything.

text: Catalogs: define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reference it everywhere
quote: Define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reference it as "catalog:" everywhere. One line to upgrade, and no more version-drift merge conflicts.

text: workspace: protocol refuses to resolve to anything other than a local workspace package
quote: pnpm supports the workspace: protocol. When this protocol is used, pnpm will refuse to resolve to anything other than a local workspace package.

text: Install fails when a workspace: version range isn't present in the workspace
quote: if you set "foo": "workspace:2.0.0", this time installation will fail because "foo@2.0.0" isn't present in the workspace

text: workspace: dependencies are replaced with real versions on publish, so no intermediate publish steps are needed
quote: This feature allows you to depend on your local workspace packages while still being able to publish the resulting packages to the remote registry without needing intermediary publish steps

text: Dry-run resolution reports what an install would change without writing anything to disk
quote: Run a full dependency resolution and report what a real install would change, without writing anything to disk. No lockfile, manifest, or `node_modules` changes are saved.

text: Offline install mode that uses only packages already in the store and fails if any are missing
quote: If true, pnpm will use only packages already available in the store. If a package won't be found locally, the installation will fail.

text: Verifies ECDSA registry signatures of installed packages against registry-published public keys
quote: Verifies the ECDSA registry signatures of installed packages against the public keys published by each registry at `/-/npm/v1/keys`.

text: Overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml can force non-vulnerable dependency versions
quote: Add overrides to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file in order to force non-vulnerable versions of the dependencies.

text: Switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically when running in CI
quote: When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.

text: In CI, install fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update
quote: In a CI environment, installation fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update.

text: Per-package project-specific configuration for workspace packages, replacing per-project .npmrc files
quote: Allows setting project-specific configuration for individual workspace packages. This replaces workspace project-specific `.npmrc` files.

text: node_modules files are hard-linked from one content-addressable store, so each version is stored once on disk
quote: Files inside node_modules are hard-linked from a single content-addressable store. A hundred projects on the same version cost you one copy on disk.

text: Updating a package adds only changed files to the store instead of copying the whole package
quote: `pnpm update` will only add 1 new file to the store, instead of cloning the entire dependency just for the singular change.

text: Dependency install scripts are blocked by default and run only for packages you approve
quote: Install scripts don't run for arbitrary dependencies. You approve which packages may execute build scripts — supply-chain safety without extra tooling.

text: List dependency licenses with pnpm licenses list
quote: Listing licenses ✅ ❌ `pnpm licenses list`

text: Generate an SBOM with pnpm sbom
quote: SBOM generation ✅ ✅ `pnpm sbom`, `npm sbom`.

text: Ships as a self-contained executable that needs no Node.js and can install the runtime itself
quote: It needs no Node.js. pnpm is a self-contained executable, and it can install the runtime for you afterwards with `pnpm runtime set node lts -g`

text: Automatically switches to the pnpm version given in the packageManager or devEngines.packageManager field
quote: If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use

text: Option to skip installing runtime entries such as Node.js from devEngines.runtime, leaving the lockfile intact
quote: Skip installing runtime entries (e.g. Node.js downloaded via `devEngines.runtime`). The lockfile is left untouched, so frozen installs still validate; only the runtime fetch and bin-linking are skipped.

text: Audit installed packages for known vulnerabilities, with auto-fix via pnpm audit --fix
quote: Checks for known security issues with the installed packages... run `pnpm audit --fix`.

text: Interactively review the advisories chosen by audit --fix and pick which to apply
quote: Review the advisories selected by `--fix` and pick which ones to apply.

text: Ignore specific vulnerabilities by GHSA ID, saved in pnpm-workspace.yaml
quote: Ignore a vulnerability by its GitHub advisory ID (GHSA). The ID is saved in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`

text: Output the audit report in JSON format
quote: Output audit report in JSON format.

text: Claims to be up to 2x faster than alternatives, backed by a published benchmark
quote: Up to 2x faster than the alternatives (see [benchmark](#benchmark)).

text: --update-checksums opt-in to accept changed tarball checksums after verification
quote: --update-checksums is the narrowly-scoped opt-in for the legitimate case (e.g. a registry rewrote its tarballs and you've verified the new bytes are correct).

text: Option to skip installing devDependencies and remove any that are already installed
quote: If `true`, pnpm will not install any package listed in `devDependencies` and will remove those insofar they were already installed.

text: Pipelined installs: each package advances to the next stage without waiting for the others
quote: Each package moves to the next stage as soon as it is ready, without waiting for the other packages.

text: Hoisted nodeLinker option creates an npm/Yarn Classic-style flat node_modules
quote: set the nodeLinker setting to `hoisted`. This will instruct pnpm to create a node_modules directory that is similar to those created by npm and Yarn Classic.

text: Auto-creates pnpm-workspace.yaml from existing workspace patterns and links projects in the same install
quote: When such a repository has no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm install` creates one with the same patterns and links the listed projects on that same install

text: Version and release workspace packages with pnpm change and pnpm version -r
quote: pnpm versions and releases workspace packages with `pnpm change` and `pnpm version -r`.

text: Lockfile-only mode updates pnpm-lock.yaml and package.json without touching node_modules
quote: When used, only updates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `package.json`. Nothing gets written to the `node_modules` directory.

text: Automatically fixes broken lockfile entries
quote: Fix broken lockfile entries automatically.

text: Configurable lockfile directory so several projects can share one lockfile
quote: The directory in which `pnpm-lock.yaml` is created. Several projects can share one lockfile.

text: Config files support ${NAME} environment variable substitution with default values
quote: Values in the configuration files may contain env variables using the `${NAME}` syntax. The env variables may also be specified with default values.

text: Supports Windows, Linux, and macOS
quote: Works everywhere. Supports Windows, Linux, and macOS.
